name: RedKitten
iocPatterns: Domain netvigil.org delivering identical HTML content across campaigns
Telegram API endpoints used for C2
Executable files such as FMAPP.dll, FMAPP.exe, burn.exe, sh.exe, AnyDesk.exe, gshdoc.exe
keyCapabilities: Exploit publicly disclosed vulnerabilities (e.g., Microsoft Excel)
Custom backdoor malware: CHAR, GhostBackDoor, HTTP_VIP
Command and control via Telegram API and cloud‑protected domains
Delivery of ransomware via lightweight loader
Use of portable executables, .NET binaries, Meterpreter, Pupy RAT, IRC bots
Third‑party C2 servers: Magic Hound, MPKBot
Exfiltration over web services (e.g., Telegram, Google Drive)
recommendedActions: Enforce a strict macro policy and monitor Office document execution
Deploy anti‑phishing email filters to block spear‑phishing with malicious macros
Block outbound traffic to Telegram API endpoints used for command and control
Prevent connections to known malicious domains (promoverse.org, netvigil.org) and associated IPs
Apply timely patches for public‑facing applications and Office vulnerabilities
Detect and block known backdoor families including CHAR, GhostBackDoor, HTTP_VIP
Monitor exfiltration tools like RClone and enforce DLP policies
Enable multi‑factor authentication and restrict RDP exposure to mitigate brute‑force attacks
Deploy EDR capable of detecting Meterpreter, Pupy, IRC bots
Implement network segmentation to limit lateral movement
campaignsText: RedKitten’s operational tempo is rapid, deploying new threats within weeks and re‑using established infrastructure across campaigns. The actor consistently targets both high‑profile institutions (government, energy) and less technically defensive NGOs, exploiting common software in many sectors. Campaigns are usually launched with macro attacks that embed exploitation code or loaders; once inside the victim network the group establishes persistence via custom backdoors and deploys ransomware to monetize the breach. High‑value intelligence is extracted through credential dumping and exfiltration over cloud services, while Android malware extends reach into mobile devices used by activists.
description: RedKitten is a highly sophisticated Iranian-linked APT that blends cyber‑espionage and ransomware capabilities to target NGOs, activists and a broad spectrum of industries worldwide. The group relies on spear‑phishing macro attachments, cloud‑protected command‑and‑control channels via Telegram, and automated exploitation of newly disclosed public vulnerabilities. Its operations show a clear mix of political data‑collection objectives with opportunistic financial gains through ransomware deployments.
goals: Strategically, RedKitten seeks dual gains: extracting politically sensitive data from Iranian human‑rights NGOs and activists to influence domestic policy, while also monetizing compromised systems through ransomware. Its target profile is globally diversified—encompassing government, critical infrastructure, finance, health, and media sectors—but it shows a pronounced focus on entities connected to Iran or its diaspora. By infecting both large corporations and smaller non‑profit organizations, the actor can harvest large volumes of data for intelligence purposes while selecting high‑value targets for financial exploitation.
